# B01 — Build a supervisor that does not trust “done”

[START](../../guide/00-START.md). Depends: B00. Outcome: a forgetful worker can resume safely.

Planned files: `scripts/build-supervisor.ts`, `tests/build/supervisor.test.ts`, package script entries and ignore rules. Read existing scripts/tests before adding dependencies; use existing Node/TypeScript/Zod where possible.

## Slices

- **s1:** Validate PLAN/CHECKPOINT schemas, unique IDs, dependencies and cycles. Select the first eligible unfinished slice. Test malformed state, missing card and circular dependencies.
- **s2:** Implement atomic checkpoint replace, source/test fingerprints and evidence verification. Test stale evidence, missing logs, forged success with nonzero exit and interrupted checkpoint writes.
- **s3:** Implement exclusive slice leases and bounded work packets. Measure token budget through an explicitly selected tokenizer or conservative configurable limit; unknown tokenizer means no exact-fit claim. Emit only named source sections; oversized packets require subdivision.
- **s4:** Add bounded command execution and a worker adapter. Protocol: packet JSON in; changed-files/evidence/blocker JSON out. An external agent runner invokes the worker and can relaunch it; no provider-specific agent SDK is assumed. Cap attempts, wall time and cost. Test worker death/resume and user stop.

Proposed CLI operations are `next`, `record`, `verify`, `resume`; define and test their exact options before documenting installation commands. They do not exist yet.

## Gate

A lying worker cannot mark a slice verified without valid test evidence. A fresh worker resumes the same unfinished slice after simulated death. Two workers cannot own it simultaneously. Verification of behavior still depends on substantive tests and review, not hashes alone.

Next: B02/s1. Keep checkpoints lightweight; full logs stay outside context.
